title: The ghazal form
hookLine: couplets, a refrain, and the poet's name in the last couplet
tomorrow: a weaver three religions claim as theirs. whose is he?

lines: PUT YOUR NAME IN THE LAST ONE.
cards: The long night is tonight: candles, fruit, Ray's old library book, Theo pretending he isn't nervous. Zoe has written two couplets of her own to read.
Ray reads them over her shoulder and says: put your name in the last one. She thinks he's teasing. He isn't.
That's yesterday's question answered, and it's the rule of the ghazal.

teach.b: A ghazal is built of couplets, and each couplet stands on its own, like a bead on a string.
At the end of each couplet comes the radif, a refrain, the same word or phrase every time, with a rhyme just before it. That's the knock in Rumi's last ghazal: reha kon, mobtala kon.

teach.h: TAKHALLUS: THE NAME IN THE LAST LINE.
teach.b: And in the last couplet, the poet signs his pen name, the takhallus, often speaking to himself.

Hafiz does it at the end of his very first ghazal: Hafiz, if you want presence, don't be absent from Him; when you meet the one you long for, let the world go. That signature carries a real Sufi teaching.
The word is hozur, presence: to be with God, not elsewhere in your head. The poet's own name becomes a reminder he can't dodge.
So Zoe's two couplets get a refrain, and in the last line, her own name, telling herself the truth.

how: Persian, Urdu and Turkish poets write ghazals in couplets with a refrain (radif) and a rhyme, and sign the last couplet with a pen name (takhallus). Hafiz's ghazals are recited and sung in that shape.

o: a long story poem told in rhymed quatrains
couplets with a refrain, signed by name at the end
a short poem chanted to a single drumbeat

games.q: the parts of a ghazal, and a week of Hafiz: tap the pairs.
p: the refrain at the end of each couplet
the pen name in the last couplet
presence: don't be absent from Him

s: in a ghazal, each couplet can stand on its own
like beads on a string, held together by the refrain and the rhyme.
a ghazal's poet signs his name in the first line
it goes in the last couplet, the takhallus, often spoken to himself.
the viral sun-and-earth line is in Hafiz's Divan
it comes from a modern book of versions. not Hafiz.

games.q: a friend writes a ghazal for her grandfather's birthday, every couplet ending on 'still here.' where should her own name go?
o: in the last couplet, speaking to herself by name.
in the title, so everyone knows who wrote it.
nowhere; naming yourself in a poem is vain.
games.why: that's the takhallus. Hafiz signs his last couplets by talking to himself: Hafiz, don't be absent from Him.

practice: Write two couplets by hand, each ending on the same short refrain, a few words like still here or tonight. In the last line, put your own name, and say something true to yourself, the way Hafiz did.

wordCard.voice: The ghazal form: couplets that stand alone, a refrain at the end of each, and the poet's own name in the last.

orig.note: Persian, from Arabic: the pen name a poet signs in a ghazal's last couplet.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: my couplets, signed in the last line. Hafiz, all eight days, done.
